question.text: A short straddle is profitable when:

answer.text: The underlying stays near the strike price (low volatility)
The underlying makes a large move in either direction

explanation.text: The Logic: A short straddle is the opposite of a long straddle — sell a call and a put at the same strike. It is used when currency prices are expected not to move much or to remain stable, so the seller collects the total premium received as maximum profit when the spot stays near the strike at expiry. The Trap: A short straddle has limited profit but unlimited loss if the exchange rate moves significantly in either direction. Note: Source: NISM-Series-I Currency Derivatives workbook, pp.109-111.
